Fifth Derivatives of a Structural Term's Predictor, in Three Directions

Source: R/structural.R
term_fifth.Rd

Returns term_fourth() differentiated once more along a third direction, with the contractions of every lower order along the three directions.

Usage

term_fifth(term, eta, y, score, psi, g, seed, blocks_data, directions, ...)

Arguments

term

A built term.

eta

The static part of the predictor.

y

The response.

score

The score callback of term_filter(), which gives the value of the driving score.

psi

The term's parameters, named as term_params().

g

The weights against which the fifth derivative is contracted, one per observation.

seed

The derivative of the static predictor in the caller's unknowns.

blocks_data

The model's derivative arrays, as set out above.

directions

A list of three numeric vectors, the directions \(v\), \(w\) and \(x\) in the caller's unknowns. The result is symmetric in the three.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A list with jacobian, the derivative of the predictor in the caller's unknowns; dphi, a list of three, the second derivative contracted against each direction; dpsi, a list of three, the third derivative contracted against the pairs \((v,w)\), \((v,x)\) and \((w,x)\); domega, the fourth derivative contracted against the three directions; each of these with one row per observation; and curvature, the fifth derivative contracted against g and the three directions.

Details

The fifth derivative of the predictor is contracted against three directions \(v\), \(w\) and \(x\) and the caller's weights, which leaves an \(m \times m\) matrix, as at the orders below. The full derivative is never formed: the recursion propagates one matrix per subset of the three directions.

Each order of differentiation of the predictor involves one more order of the family, so this order reads the family's sixth derivative. Unlike the orders below, the model's derivatives are given as arrays rather than as a callback, because the contractions that the fifth order forms from them are many: blocks_data is a list with H, D3, D4, D5 and D6, the derivatives of the driving score in the predictors of every equation, of orders one to five, one row per observation (H one column per parameter, D3 one column per pair of parameters at (a - 1) * npar + b, and so on, as for the compiled routes of term_fourth()); Vs, a list of the Jacobian rows of every equation, one n by m matrix per parameter (the filter's own entry is not read); and ap, the index of the filter's own parameter.

The base method returns zeros, which is correct for a term whose predictor is a block of columns times coefficients. A structural term signals an error, for the reason that term_third() gives.

See also

term_fourth() for the order below.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(t = 1:20, y = rnorm(20))
term <- term_build(linpar(~t), dd)
# an additive term bends no predictor, so every order above the first is
# zero, as the base method returns
out <- term_fifth(term, rep(0, 20), dd$y,
                  score = function(e, i) dd$y[i] - e, psi = list(),
                  g = rep(1, 20), seed = matrix(0, 20, 2),
                  blocks_data = NULL,
                  directions = list(c(1, 0), c(0, 1), c(1, 1)))
all(out$curvature == 0)
#> [1] TRUE
